test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Under which of the following Acts of British India did the British government take direct control of the administration of India in its own hands?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act 1858**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Government of India Act 1858** was the legislation that marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and transferred the control of India to the British Crown.
 
• This act was enacted in response to the Indian Rebellion of 1857, which exposed the vulnerabilities and inadequacies of the Company's administration.
 
• Under this Act, the British government established the office of the Secretary of State for India, who was given complete authority and control over the Indian administration.
 
• The Act also led to the creation of the India Council to assist the Secretary of State for India.
 
• This transition marked the beginning of the period known as the British Raj, which lasted until India's independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Prior to the Government of India Act 1858, the East India Company had been the ruling entity in India, having gained significant control after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.
 
• The Act was also known as the Act for the Better Government of India and was passed on August 2, 1858.
 
• It led to the establishment of the office of Viceroy of India, a position held by the Governor-General of India, who acted as the representative of the British Crown.
 
• The Act aimed to improve the governance of India by ensuring a more direct and accountable administration under the British Parliament.
 
• The administrative structure set up by this Act remained largely unchanged until the passage of the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy and federal structure.
